analysis: All supplied changes are documentation-only. CHANGELOG.md units 12 and 13 are head-text excerpts of existing release notes; no executable code, config, or protocol behavior is changed in them. In docs/provider/cli-reference.md, the patch (unit 1) bumps the freshness stamp from 2026-10-02 to 2026-10-05 and adds a paragraph in the 'LaunchAgent environment passthrough' section. The paragraph says TMPDIR selects the anonymous runtime metallib snapshot directory for sandboxed foreground/local startup and is not forwarded to the background provider, and it links to reference/configuration.md#runtime-metallib-snapshots. Unit 0 for the same file has no text, only metadata (modified, mode 100644 on both sides), so it carries no security content. The security-relevant claim in the new paragraph is the TMPDIR/metallib snapshot behavior (relevant to TB-003 and T-013/T-034 runtime-integrity), but the underlying code change is not in the supplied batch, so I could not check the documented behavior against the implementation. The next pass should check the corresponding provider source: whether the TMPDIR path is validated, whether snapshots are anonymous and unlinked, whether a symlink or world-writable directory could allow a metallib swap, and whether the runtime manifest hash is verified after the snapshot. This is a coverage limit, not evidence that the change is safe. No threat model assumptions are invalidated by the docs alone.
